counterfactual.change: reduced dt from 0.03333 to 0.001 (one field); same 2 steps; energy stays ~1120 and no violation, showing failure is large-dt gravity integration error

explanation: Free-falling body with no walls/collisions or controller gains ~226 J in 2 steps at dt=1/30. vy falls 30->34->38 (delta 4 per step) while g*dt is only 0.667, so gravity is over-applied ~6x. Semi-implicit Euler alone would gain only m*g^2*dt^2~0.4 J/step. The shrunk trace reports 50-53 substeps per step, indicating fast-body substepping interacts with gravity (e.g. full-dt gravity per substep or velocity-dependent substep count feeding back), pumping kinetic energy faster than potential loss.
vision_note: A lone blue body falls vertically with no walls, other bodies, or waypoints visible. It drops an abnormally large distance between step 0 and step 2, indicating far too much downward velocity gain.
